title: FOXJ1 transcriptional targets in human airway cells and impaired multiciliogenesis in FOXJ1-associated primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Thomas, Lucie; Serizay, Jacques; Mani, Rahma; Couvet, Sandrine; Papon, Jean-Francois; Tamalet, Aline; Mitri, Rana; Faucon, Catherine; Murris-Espin, Marlene; Blanchard, Emmanuelle; Langeois, Maud; Blesson, Sophie; Tissier, Sylvie; Montantin, Guy; Moal, Florence Dastot-Le; Levergeois, Romain; Louis, Bruno; Beydon, Nicole; Thouvenin, Guillaume; Escudier, Estelle; Amselem, Serge; Giurgea, Irina; Zaragosi, Laure-Emmanuelle; Meunier, Alice; Legendre, Marie
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过ChIP-seq和RNA-seq研究FOXJ1在人类气道细胞中的转录靶点，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点鉴定，但缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，且未聚焦三维互作建模，仅属边缘相关。
abstract: Fluid mobilization on epithelia is ensured by the motile cilia of differentiated multiciliated cells (MCCs). Key transcriptional regulators of motile ciliogenesis include CCNO, MCIDAS, RFXs, and the transcription factor FOXJ1, whose precise role in humans remains unclear. We show that, unlike CCNO and MCIDAS, FOXJ1 expression persists in well-differentiated human airway epithelial cells (hAECs), suggesting functions beyond cilia initiation. ChIP-seq in hAECs allowed us to refine the consensus target motifs of FOXJ1 and RFXs, as well as their close proximity, which strongly suggests functional cooperation within a transcriptional complex. By combining ChIP-seq in normal cells with RNAseq from patients with FOXJ1-related primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), we identified 683 direct FOXJ1 target genes. Among these, 89 MCC-enriched genes-particularly those encoding axonemal proteins such as microtubule-inner proteins (MIPs) and dynein arm docking components-were downregulated in FOXJ1-deficient cells. Collectively, these findings provide new insights into how FOXJ1 contributes to human motile ciliogenesis, and reveal a potential role for FOXJ1 in maintaining MCCs differentiation and ciliary function by sustaining the expression of ciliary proteins, particularly those in direct contact with axonemal tubulin.
abstract_zh: 上皮组织上的液体动员由分化多纤毛细胞（MCCs）的运动纤毛确保。运动纤毛生成的关键转录调控因子包括CCNO、MCIDAS、RFXs及转录因子FOXJ1，其在人类中的精确作用仍不清楚。我们表明，与CCNO和MCIDAS不同，FOXJ1表达在充分分化的人气道上皮细胞（hAECs）中持续存在，提示其功能超越纤毛起始。在hAECs中的ChIP-seq使我们能够细化FOXJ1和RFXs的共识靶标基序及其紧密邻近性，这强烈暗示它们在一个转录复合物内的功能协作。通过将正常细胞中的ChIP-seq与FOXJ1相关原发性纤毛运动障碍（PCD）患者的RNAseq相结合，我们鉴定了683个FOXJ1直接靶基因。其中，89个MCC富集基因——特别是编码轴丝蛋白如微管内蛋白（MIPs）和动力蛋白臂对接组件的基因——在FOXJ1缺陷细胞中下调。总体而言，这些发现为FOXJ1如何促进人类运动纤毛生成提供了新见解，并揭示了FOXJ1通过维持纤毛蛋白（尤其是与轴丝微管蛋白直接接触的蛋白）表达，在维持MCCs分化和纤毛功能中的潜在作用。
